intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene.

checks.claim: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants
checks.explanation: The paper links axonal sensorimotor neuropathy to homozygous MPV17 variants. It never uses the name CMT2EE, which is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with juvenile or adult onset. It causes distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs, along with distal sensory loss and absent tendon reflexes. Unlike Navajo neurohepatopathy, which is also caused by MPV17 mutations, it occurs without hepatic or brain involvement (Choi et al., 2015; Baumann et al., 2019).

checks.claim: CMT2EE is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: This study enrolled two autosomal recessive Korean families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (FC26 and FC355, Fig. 1a).

checks.claim: CMT2EE has juvenile or adult onset.
checks.evidence_quote: MPV17 mutations in juvenile- and adult-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.explanation: The title states juvenile- and adult-onset.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: Neurologic examination at the age of 34 years revealed muscle weakness and atrophies of bilateral, distal muscles, predominantly in the lower limbs.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes distal sensory loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Vibration and position senses were more severely disturbed than pain and touch senses.
checks.explanation: Sensory disturbance and absent SNAPs are reported, but 'distal' sensory loss is not explicitly described.

checks.claim: CMT2EE causes absent tendon reflexes.
checks.evidence_quote: Deep tendon reflexes, in all extremities, were absent.

checks.claim: Navajo neurohepatopathy is also caused by MPV17 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in MPV17 cause the autosomal recessive disorder mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 6 (MTDPS6), also called Navajo neurohepatopathy (NNH).

checks.claim: Unlike Navajo neurohepatopathy, CMT2EE occurs without hepatic or brain involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast to previously reported NNH patients, the patients presented here exhibited only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without liver and brain symptoms.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) reported a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, whose walking difficulties began at age 14 years. Over several years these progressed to bilateral foot drop requiring orthoses, with symmetric distal numbness and coldness in the feet rising to the knees, and milder numbness in the hands. Examination showed wasting of the hands and distal lower limbs, clawed toes, a slow unsteady gait, decreased tone, and severe distal weakness. There was symmetric weakness of hip flexion, and all tendon reflexes were absent. Pinprick and light touch perception were decreased distal to the knees, vibration sense was impaired to the ankles, and joint position sense was absent at the toes. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Sural nerve biopsy showed a severe chronic axonal neuropathy with only occasional surviving myelinated axons. Unlike later reported patients, this patient also had extraneural involvement. Brain MRI showed diffuse T2 hyperintensity in the cerebral white matter and cerebellum, consistent with leukoencephalopathy. CSF protein (1963 mg/L) and lactate (4.3 mmol/L) were increased. He had mild hepatomegaly, and liver biopsy showed patchy steatosis with early bridging fibrosis, although there was no clinically significant chronic liver disease. Cognition was not significantly impaired. Muscle biopsy showed ragged-red fibers, about 20% cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-deficient fibers, and subsarcolemmal accumulation of abnormal mitochondria with parking lot-like inclusions. Long-range PCR detected multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle, but mtDNA copy number was normal. His sister had died of a progressive hepatitis at age 9 years. Blakely et al. (2012) noted that the patient's phenotype resembled the classic form of Navajo neurohepatopathy.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) reported 2 patients from 2 unrelated Korean families, each born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents, who had axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without liver or brain involvement. Patient 1 was a 34-year-old woman. She first noticed distal lower limb weakness at age 9 years and began walking with short leg braces at age 12. On examination she had bilateral distal weakness and atrophy, predominantly in the lower limbs, and severe atrophy of the intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles. She also had flexion deformities of the interphalangeal joints, ankle joint deformity, and scoliosis. Vibration and position senses were more severely affected than pain and touch, and knee and ankle jerks were absent. Patient 2 was a 22-year-old man who first had gait and balance problems at age 13 years and began using short leg braces at age 20. He had distal weakness and atrophy, flat feet, atrophy of the intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles, a similar pattern of sensory disturbance, and absent deep tendon reflexes. Neither patient had growth retardation, gastrointestinal dysmotility, hepatomegaly, cognitive impairment, ophthalmoplegia, corneal scarring, or hypoglycemic attacks. Serum lactate was mildly elevated in both (2.1 and 1.9 mmol/L), but liver enzymes were normal. In both patients, electrophysiologic studies showed decreased motor conduction velocities and CMAPs in the median and ulnar nerves. Peroneal and tibial CMAPs and all sensory nerve action potentials were absent, and sural nerve responses were lost early in the disease. Visual and brainstem auditory evoked potentials were normal. Brain MRI was normal. Lower leg MRI showed severe atrophy and fatty replacement, predominantly of the soleus muscles, with relative sparing of the tibialis posterior and lateral gastrocnemius muscles; this pattern was consistent with length-dependent axonal degeneration. Sural nerve biopsy from patient 1 showed nearly complete loss of large and medium-sized myelinated fibers without demyelination or onion bulbs. Vastus lateralis biopsy from patient 2 showed a few ragged-red fibers and subsarcolemmal accumulation of enlarged mitochondria.

paragraphs.text: In a 21-year-old Pakistani man with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, leukoencephalopathy, and liver involvement, Blakely et al. (2012) sequenced the POLG, DGUOK, and MPV17 genes and identified a homozygous missense mutation in MPV17: pro98-to-leu (P98L). The paper gives the nucleotide change as c.298C-T in a figure legend and as c.2898C-T in the text. The mutation affected a residue conserved from human to yeast and had previously been reported in a patient with mtDNA depletion in the liver. Parental samples were not available.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Korean patients from 2 unrelated families with axonal CMT2EE, Choi et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing and identified a homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene, resulting in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution at a residue conserved across vertebrates. The mutation, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, was apparently inherited from each parent. It was not found in 300 controls or in 302 in-house exomes, but was present at very low frequency in the Exome Sequencing Project (0.00008) and ExAC (0.00002471) databases. In NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells, siRNA knockdown of MPV17 significantly reduced cell proliferation and viability against reactive oxygen species and affected OXPHOS levels. Overexpression of the R41Q mutant significantly inhibited cell proliferation. Choi et al. (2015) suggested that both loss of normal MPV17 function and a detrimental effect of the mutant protein may contribute to neuronal dysfunction.

paragraphs.text: In 5 patients from 2 unrelated families with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy without hepatocerebral involvement, Baumann et al. (2019) identified homozygous mutations in the MPV17 gene. The affected members of the first family carried the c.122G-A (R41Q) mutation. Those of the second family carried a novel near-splice mutation (c.376-9T-G), which was shown to cause an in-frame deletion of 11 amino acids.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) noted that both R41Q and the arg50-to-gln (R50Q) mutation found in Navajo neurohepatopathy affect residues in the matrix region between the first 2 transmembrane domains of MPV17, although the 2 mutations cause quite different clinical phenotypes. In NSC34 cells, overexpression of a different substitution at the same residue (R41W) also affected cell proliferation. From these data, Choi et al. (2015) proposed that mutations at arg41 predominantly cause peripheral neuropathy.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Onset in first or second decade
Distal muscle atrophy, including intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles
Fatty infiltration of soleus muscles on MRI
Loss of large and medium myelinated fibers on sural nerve biopsy
clinical_synopsis.hpo_label: Decreased number of large peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials

paragraphs.text: In a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, Blakely et al. (2012) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the MPV17 gene that resulted in a pro98-to-leu (P98L) substitution at a residue conserved from human to yeast. The paper gives the nucleotide change as c.298C-T in a figure legend and as c.2898C-T in the text. The patient had adult-presenting axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, leukoencephalopathy, and liver involvement, along with multiple mtDNA deletions and focal COX deficiency in skeletal muscle. The mutation had previously been reported in a patient with hepatic mtDNA depletion. Parental samples were not available.

paragraphs.text: In 2 patients from 2 unrelated nonconsanguineous Korean families with axonal CMT2EE, Choi et al. (2015) identified a homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene, resulting in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution at a conserved residue. The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. It was not found in 300 controls or in 302 in-house exomes, but was present at very low frequency in the ESP and ExAC databases. Overexpressing the mutant protein in NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells significantly inhibited cell proliferation.
